section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1998
title: 2.10 MEANS ADOPTED FOR COMMITTING SUICIDES 2.10.1 The means adopted for suicides varied from the easily available or exercisable means such as consumption of poison, jumping into the well etc. to the more painful means such as self inflicted injuries, hanging, shooting etc. to commit suicide. Hanging (25.6%), Consumption of insecticides (18.2%) and Consumption of other poisons (19.1%) were the more used means to end one's life. While the share of committing suicide by 'Hanging' has decreased (from 26.71 in 1997 to 25.6% in 1998), the same due poisoning has increased (from 36.7% in 1997 to 37.3% in 1998). Table-2.10
